## Framing

The design is closer to “add a third adapter” than “add a table row”: HEAD’s non-codex retry/repair paths and the argv contract are still agy-specific (findings #1-#2). Read-only is also being framed only as write safety. A scratch tree would not fix the other exposure: native `read_file` may still read outside the repository, and the contributor model’s training policy is a confidentiality decision, not a sandbox decision.

### Q1
Do not add a scratch workspace by default. It would weaken review fidelity (a copy can drift, and untracked/ignored files are easy to omit) while adding synchronization and quota cost. Keep the Muse preventive flags, run in the repository root, and retain the before/after evidence check. Document the real boundary: gitignored paths, submodules, and files outside the repository remain unmonitored; the launcher/updater can also write outside the tree. A stronger option is an OS-level read-only mount/container or disposable VM, but that is a separate, portable-infrastructure project. To choose, I would need Muse’s actual tool filesystem scope, updater behavior, and the threat model for secrets versus integrity.

### Q2
Refusing is the safer default. Better still, make the first version subscription-only and refuse both known API-key variables regardless of `-SkipPreflight`; API-key billing belongs in a Codex provider, not this engine. If coexistence is essential, do not merely delete two names: launch Muse with an explicit allowlisted child environment, preserve keys only for an explicit API-key entry, and record the sanitization. That avoids unknown future key aliases and surprise account selection.

### Q3
A local `auth.json` shape check is acceptable and preferable to spending one of only 10-50 prompts. Call it “credential file present,” not proof of validity; an expired token should fail on the real run and be classified auth. Also, keychain mode cannot be a mere warning in the current preflight model: it is `unknown` and is refused unless explicitly overridden. A non-consuming `muse auth/status` command, if one exists, would be better.

### Q4
Fragile parts are the MSP envelope/version, nested `stream` selection, `run.model.configured`, and the precise terminal payload. Parse semantics, not record luck: require a supported `schema_version`, one session stream with a UUID, terminal and session on that stream, exactly one terminal, and a configured model equal to the requested model. Map exit 2 and max-steps to explicit capability failures rather than leaving them `unknown`. Record a real CLI/MSP version using a non-billing command; optionally pin `muse-bin-<version>.exe` via `CODEX_CONSULT_MUSE_EXE`, and fail closed on an unsupported MSP version rather than silently trusting the auto-updating `muse.cmd`.

## Verified versus inferred

Verified at HEAD: engine table and adapter contract, argv construction, preflight/roster validation, endpoint fingerprinting, shared failure classifier, tree snapshots, retry/repair calls, panel propagation, provider listing, and test surface. Inferred from the brief or not covered by its probes: Muse resume session identity, version/auth subcommands, launcher behavior for paths with spaces or `%`, out-of-repository `read_file`, and whether every listed 1.2 model is subscription-eligible.

findings.claim: The generic non-codex denial-retry and format-repair paths hardcode the agy event parser and outcome, so a newly added muse adapter would work only on the first turn and misparse every retry or repair turn.
findings.trigger: A muse run returns prose despite the native schema, or returns an empty denial-like terminal, with the current retry defaults enabled.

evidence.observation: The first turn calls the adapter, but retry and repair call Read-AgyEvents and Get-AgyTurnOutcome directly; the catch fallback is also Read-AgyEvents.

findings.verification: Run a fake-muse prose reply with -FormatRetry 1 and inspect whether the second MSP stream is parsed and committed as a muse reply.
findings.remedy: Route every turn through engineSpec.Adapter.Events/Outcome, or explicitly disable denial and format retries for muse and test that policy.

findings.claim: The current adapter argv contract cannot launch Muse as designed: it passes only model, schema path, thread and native effort, while Muse additionally needs the prompt-file path, max-model-steps and effort on every run.
findings.trigger: Adding the proposed muse row without first extending the adapter interface and main argv construction.

evidence.observation: The main run builds adapter argv from four fields and writes the adapter stdin text to a temp file; no prompt path or step limit reaches the adapter.

findings.verification: With a fake muse, dry-run the engine and assert the exact exec argv contains the prompt file, schema, effort and max-step values.
findings.remedy: Pass an engine turn-options object (prompt path, schema, thread, effort, max steps) to the adapter, and define muse Stdin as the raw prompt or remove stdin for this engine.

findings.claim: The roster format currently rejects both the muse engine value and the proposed per-entry billing key, and the design does not define validation, persistence, or panel-child propagation for that key.
findings.trigger: A roster containing {"engine":"muse"} or {"billing":"api-key"} at HEAD.

evidence.observation: Entry keys are limited to provider/model/codex_config/auth/panel/engine, engine must belong to EngineNames, and only codex and agy are listed.

findings.verification: Validate a muse roster with and without the billing key and a -Panel member; all three paths must accept or reject it consistently.
findings.remedy: Extend EngineNames and the roster schema deliberately, validate billing as subscription|api-key, carry it into the entry and panel spec, and record it in the ledger.

findings.claim: The billing guard has no defined integration point; if it is treated as an ordinary preflight check, -SkipPreflight can bypass it, roster walking may not skip subscription muse entries, and panel children may repeat the decision inconsistently.
findings.trigger: META_API_KEY or MODEL_API_KEY is set and a muse run is launched with -SkipPreflight, a roster walk, or -Panel.

evidence.observation: Unknown credentials are refused only by preflight and -SkipPreflight is documented to bypass credential refusals; the child is launched with the inherited environment.

findings.verification: Set each key and run muse with -SkipPreflight, as a roster walk, and as a panel member; every subscription attempt must refuse before launch and fallback behavior must be explicit.
findings.remedy: Make billing an independent fail-closed launch invariant evaluated for the selected entry and again immediately before Start-Process; expose it in provider listings and never allow -SkipPreflight to override it.

findings.claim: Letting some muse entries opt into API-key billing while every muse entry shares cc-engine-v1|muse would commingle unrelated endpoint health: an API-key auth, quota or billing failure can block the signed-in subscription and vice versa.
findings.trigger: One muse roster entry uses billing=api-key and another uses the subscription, then either mode records an auth or quota failure.

evidence.observation: Every non-codex engine has one static fingerprint derived only from the engine name; Get-EndpointHealth is keyed by that fingerprint.

findings.verification: Seed ledger health for one billing mode and run preflight for the other; the design must either isolate them or justify shared health.
findings.remedy: Initially support subscription only; otherwise include the billing route in the endpoint identity and adjust thread-drift rules accordingly.

findings.claim: A keychain-backend result described merely as a warning does not fit the current preflight state machine: unknown sign-in is a refusal unless -SkipPreflight is passed, not an available-with-warning outcome.
findings.trigger: Muse credentials are in the OS keychain and no recent usable muse ledger entry exists.

evidence.observation: Get-PreflightVerdict maps credential State unknown to unavailable/unknown refusal text.

findings.verification: Run the keychain configuration without a live call and inspect the roster walk and explicit-provider refusal.
findings.remedy: Return State=unknown with precise reason, or find/use a free auth-status command; do not call it a warning unless preflight gains a safe unknown-and-available category.

findings.claim: Parsing auth.json proves only the expected shape, not a valid or current sign-in; moreover a normal ConvertFrom-Json parse materializes values in memory even if they are never printed.
findings.trigger: auth.json contains providers.meta with an expired, malformed or stale OAuth value.

evidence.observation: The existing credential model explicitly says local checks cannot establish live validity; validity is learned from a failed run.
Property-name inspection still requires deserializing the containing object unless a stream-level parser is used.

findings.verification: Use a fake auth file with providers.meta but invalid token data and confirm preflight wording followed by an auth-classified run failure.
findings.remedy: Treat the check as local credential-file evidence, never log the object, and let real auth failures update endpoint health.

findings.claim: The design overstates the agy-derived check as proving that a run that changed anything fails: gitignored paths, submodules and files outside the repository are not monitored, and Muse/launcher writes to home or config locations are invisible.
findings.trigger: A reviewer or launcher writes under .gitignore, inside a submodule, or to a user-profile path during the run.

evidence.observation: The revision manifest excludes ignored paths and does not recurse submodules; the documented enforcement explicitly has these blind spots.

findings.verification: Have the fake reviewer write to a gitignored path and confirm no tree failure is recorded.
findings.remedy: State the evidence boundary exactly; add an OS sandbox/read-only mount only if the threat model requires those paths.

findings.claim: A tree mutation is forced to provider class permission only when the engine otherwise produced a usable reply; when the same run already failed, the current branch merely appends the tree problem and leaves the original failure class.
findings.trigger: Muse writes a monitored file and also exits nonzero or emits a failed terminal.

evidence.observation: Only the usable-reply branch assigns agyFailureClass=permission; the else branch appends to bridgeOutcome without changing class.

findings.verification: Fake a file write plus exit 1 and inspect provider_failure.class against the documented rule.
findings.remedy: Either force permission whenever a mutation is the safety violation, or document that the primary provider class wins with the mutation appended; add a test.

findings.claim: Reusing the agy tree-check text and sandbox ledger description unchanged would lie about muse: it would say muse’s sandbox does not block writes and restricts only the terminal, although muse is invoked with --disable-write and --disable-shell.
findings.trigger: Any muse run that changes a monitored path, or any ledger sandbox field for muse.

evidence.observation: Both strings hardcode the agy --sandbox limitation.

findings.verification: Inspect the failure message and ledger sandbox text from a fake muse write.
findings.remedy: Parameterize the enforcement description: preventive Muse flags plus bridge evidence, with the same evidence blind spots.

findings.claim: The proposed MSP extraction does not define enough stream identity invariants: any stream.kind=session record can win, multiple session streams are not rejected, the session need not match the terminal stream or be a UUID, and run.model.configured is not checked against the requested model.
findings.trigger: A CLI update emits nested/substream session records, two session records, a non-UUID id, a terminal on another stream, or a fallback model; the parser could accept the wrong thread or silently review with the contributor default.

evidence.observation: The agy precedent rejects init/result mismatches, foreign resumed conversations and non-UUID ids.
The brief records the fields but the design only says take a session record and terminal text.

findings.verification: Feed fake MSP streams with two session ids, a mismatched terminal stream, no UUID and a wrong configured model; all must fail without ingestion.
findings.remedy: Give the parser the expected thread and model, validate one consistent session stream and one terminal, and classify model drift as capability/config failure.

findings.claim: The design leaves Muse’s documented exit classes unmapped: exit 2 usage errors and exit 1 max-steps/cancellation are not matched by the shared keyword classifier unless their reason happens to contain a recognized word, so they will often be unknown.
findings.trigger: Muse exits 2 for an unknown flag, exits 1 for max model steps, or exits 130/143 without bridge-side timeout text.

evidence.observation: The classifier recognizes provider wording patterns but has no max-steps, usage-error or CLI-signal rule.

findings.verification: Run fake exit-code/reason combinations and inspect provider_failure.class and retry_after.
findings.remedy: Map exit 2 and max-steps to capability, cancellation to a defined class, signals consistently with bridge timeout/transport handling, and classify quota only from actual quota reason text.

findings.claim: The design neither pins nor detects the actual Muse binary/MSP version: Get-EngineHarness would inspect muse.cmd metadata, while the auto-updating launcher can select muse-bin-<version>.exe after that, leaving the static engine fingerprint unchanged.
findings.trigger: Muse auto-updates between the recorded harness determination and process launch, or an update changes the MSP envelope.

evidence.observation: Harness version comes from launcher file metadata and the endpoint fingerprint is only cc-engine-v1|<engine>.
muse.cmd delegates through an updating PowerShell launcher to a versioned 434 MB binary; a .cmd shim may carry no useful ProductVersion.

findings.verification: Run the version probe against muse.cmd and the resolved versioned binary and compare reviewer.harness with the record actually emitted in MSP.
findings.remedy: Use a free version command, resolve or allow pinning the versioned binary, record CLI plus MSP schema version, and fail closed outside the supported compatibility set.

findings.claim: Muse is the first non-codex engine to put both prompt and schema paths in argv through a .cmd/PowerShell launcher chain; spaces, percent-signs and launcher re-quoting are not covered by the probe.
findings.trigger: The repository, temporary directory or plugin path contains spaces or a % variable-like component.

evidence.observation: The code explicitly avoids prompt argv through codex.cmd because cmd.exe can expand %VAR% inside quotes.
No verified probe in the brief covers paths with spaces or percent signs.

findings.verification: Point CODEX_CONSULT_MUSE_EXE and the repo at temporary paths containing spaces and %APPDATA% text, then compare received and intended argv in fake-muse.
findings.remedy: Test the launcher chain and, if needed, resolve a stable executable or use ProcessStartInfo with a controlled environment and argument list.

findings.claim: The brief treats one consultation as one Muse prompt, but the bridge’s default format repair and denial retry can spend a second or third Muse prompt on the same consultation and consume the 10-50/5 h quota unexpectedly.
findings.trigger: A muse structured reply is prose, or an empty outcome resembling a denial, while FormatRetry and DenialRetry retain their defaults.

evidence.observation: Both extra turns are enabled by default for non-codex engines and launch complete engine turns.

findings.verification: Instrument fake-muse to count exec invocations for a prose first reply and assert the intended one-turn or retry budget.
findings.remedy: Disable one or both retries for muse by default, or expose and record a strict muse prompt budget; never let a retry run after quota failure.

findings.claim: The proposed -MaxModelSteps value is not included in the panel-member argument spec, so muse panel members would not inherit the operator’s limit and could diverge from solo runs.
findings.trigger: Run -Panel with one or more muse entries and a nondefault -MaxModelSteps.

evidence.observation: The serialized member args include timeout, engine and engine_exe but no max-model-steps field.

findings.verification: Dry-run/execute a muse panel member with a distinctive limit and inspect its command and ledger.
findings.remedy: Add a validated positive MaxModelSteps to parameters, dry run, panel spec and ledger command; reject it for engines that do not use it.

findings.claim: codex-providers.ps1 hardcodes its explicit -EngineExe override for agy, so the muse engine and its tests can use the environment override but cannot use the CLI’s documented generic explicit-launcher parameter.
findings.trigger: Run codex-providers.ps1 -EngineExe <path-to-fake-muse.cmd> for a muse roster entry.

evidence.observation: The parameter documentation and engineLaunchers assignment name only agy.

findings.verification: Invoke the provider listing with a fake muse launcher through -EngineExe and through CODEX_CONSULT_MUSE_EXE; compare behavior.
findings.remedy: Either document that muse uses only its environment override or add an engine-qualified explicit-launcher mechanism shared by provider listing and consultation.

findings.claim: The proposed fake/harness matrix omits several of the design’s highest-risk cases: malformed/partial JSONL, unsupported MSP schema version, multiple or mismatched session streams, wrong configured model, usage/max-step exits, keychain preflight, API-key opt-in, retry/repair parsing, panel propagation of MaxModelSteps, and billing with -SkipPreflight.
findings.trigger: Executing only the knob list in the design brief before acceptance.

evidence.observation: The existing agy fake covers analogous malformed/thread/failure knobs, while the proposed muse knob list is smaller.

findings.verification: Run the completed muse harness and confirm every listed branch has an assertion over argv, ledger class, thread and stored reply.
findings.remedy: Extend fake-muse with those knobs and add unit and end-to-end assertions before any real run is trusted.

findings.claim: The read-only flags address mutation and command execution but do not establish that native read_file is confined to the repository, so confidentiality of external files is still outside the enforcement boundary.
findings.trigger: A muse reviewer requests an absolute path outside the repository or a path traversing out of the root.

evidence.observation: The verified probe shows repository reading, not a filesystem boundary for arbitrary paths.
No probe shows that Muse rejects absolute or traversing paths.

findings.verification: In a disposable repository, ask Muse to read a marked external file and inspect the terminal answer and tree check.
findings.remedy: Document the exposure; use an OS-level filesystem sandbox if external-file confidentiality is in scope.

findings.claim: caps-v1 would declare the 1.2 muse models even though the brief verifies only the 1.3 pair under the subscription and merely says the docs list 1.2 and 1.1.
findings.trigger: A roster selects muse-spark-1.2 or its contributor variant when that model is not subscription-enabled.

evidence.observation: The fact and design sections distinguish live acceptance from documentation-only availability.

findings.verification: Run one bounded model-availability probe for each 1.2 id or obtain vendor confirmation before shipping the caps row.
findings.remedy: Declare only live-verified subscription models initially, or document that 1.2 entries are docs-declared and may fail capability preflight at runtime.

findings.claim: The default max-model-steps value of 80 is asserted without evidence that a normal code review fits, so a legitimate long review can be terminated after consuming a subscription prompt.
findings.trigger: A muse reviewer needs more than 80 model steps to inspect a large repository or answer all brief questions.

evidence.observation: Only small 20-31 second probes are recorded; no step-count distribution supports 80.

findings.verification: Collect step counts from several real bounded reviews, including a large repo, before fixing the default.
findings.remedy: Use the vendor default unless a measured safety budget is required, or set a purpose-aware limit and classify a max-steps termination explicitly.

verdict_reason: This is a framing/design consultation rather than an acceptance or diff review, and the design needs the adapter, billing, parser and test changes identified above before implementation.
unproven: Muse resume with --session-id emits the same verified session id and preserves the requested model.
Muse provides a free, non-consuming version or auth-status command, and a supported way to disable launcher auto-update.
The muse.cmd/PowerShell launcher preserves quoted prompt/schema paths containing spaces and percent-sign text.
Native read_file cannot read absolute or traversing paths outside the repository root.
Every muse-spark-1.2 model is available under the tested subscription.
